summary.headline: Cohance Q2 FY27 revenue rose 13% QoQ to Rs 4,767 mn and adjusted EBITDA reached Rs 458 mn (~10% margin), with H2 guided to grow YoY.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 recovered sequentially from a weak Q1: revenue up about 13% QoQ to Rs 4,767 mn and adjusted EBITDA up from Rs 92 mn to Rs 458 mn, with adjusted EBITDA margin near 10%. Year-on-year performance remained lower, driven by reduced Pharma CDMO and ADC contribution and adverse mix. Management reiterated that H2 FY27 should show YoY growth in both revenue and EBITDA, but the Surya Pette facility closure order, announced in the last 24 hours of the call, adds uncertainty. Specialty Chemicals guidance was cut to a YoY decline for FY27.

segments.name: Pharma CDMO (small molecules, ADC, nucleic acid)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue up 34.5% QoQ on small molecules; down 27% YoY in Q2 and 32% YoY in H1. Each technology contributed 13.7% of revenue in Q2 and 14.4% in H1. Nucleic acid (Tapala) grew 33.6% YoY in Q2 without early phase 3 supplies.

segments.name: API Plus (API and formulations)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 2,671 mn, +5% YoY, hit by heavy audit schedule and shipment timing. H1 revenue slightly below prior year; YTD material margin % ahead of last year despite higher raw material prices.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 417 mn, -40.6% YoY on lower agrochemical CDMO volumes, pricing pressure and phasing. FY27 revenue now expected to decline YoY, versus earlier guidance of broadly flat.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 expected to deliver YoY growth in both revenue and EBITDA, per management based on current visibility.
Sequential improvement expected to continue through H2; no numeric quantitative guidance given.
Specialty Chemicals FY27 revenue now expected to decline YoY (previously broadly flat).
NJ Bio targeted to approach breakeven; no further restructuring costs expected in H2 after recent transactions.
Bioconjugation capacity expansion on track for commercial availability by early FY28.
Two new small molecule commercial programs: first revenue expected Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28 (RSM deliveries).
Surya Pette impact still being assessed; management said it would guide once clarity on the timeline emerges.
capex_capacity: Bioconjugation capacity expansion on track for commercial availability by early FY28.
Additional capital programs planned over next few years for ADC payload, linker and bioconjugation capabilities; investments tied to customer visibility.
Specialty Chemicals: automation and environmental upgrades at multi-purpose agrochemical facility plus dedicated R&D lab to speed customer qualification.
Surya Pette facility (smaller, non-GMP plant) closure order received; impact under assessment.
H1 capex just over Rs 1 bn excluding acquisitions.
demand_pricing: Small molecules: multiple reload orders on existing commercial programs improve Q3, Q4 and next-year visibility; two new commercial programs and one late-stage program secured from large global pharma (all European, patent-protected products).
Phase 3 pipeline at 11 programs and commercial pipeline at 19 products, per management.
ADC: two customers destocked across established commercial programs in H1; RFQs increasing across payload and linkers, some potentially made in India.
API Plus: generic API pricing described as stable with no major rises or falls; selective price pass-through used to offset higher raw material costs on some products.
Life cycle management: innovator pricing for off-patent products said to be slightly premium to generic pricing; monetisation 18 to 36 months after sampling starts.

qa_highlights.question: Are the two new commercial projects patent protected, and what is the tech transfer lead time?
qa_highlights.answer: Both are patent-protected small molecule products from large innovators; first deliveries of RSM expected Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28. Management said this is incremental to the H2 above H1 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How long does life cycle management take from sampling to commercial, and how does pricing evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Gates include qualification, audits, sampling, validation, filing and approval; monetisation could take 18 to 36 months. Price erosion is not significant and innovator pricing is slightly above generic. Of the three pharma companies engaged, all European, two are new and one is existing.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs 260 crore of disrupted revenue at Surya Pette will be recovered in FY27 H2 and FY28, and has restocking been received?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify. Two small molecule KSMs are becoming generic, lowering volumes. One molecule still under patent received good reloads for FY27 and FY28, which supports H2 FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Subsidiary costs fell from Rs 41 crore in Q1 to nearly nil in Q2; how much is recurring savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs were limited in Q2 due to restructuring transactions completed in the last 30 to 60 days; no further such costs expected in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of FDA classification for inspected sites and any impact on H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Responses to all three FDA audits submitted; classification expected in 1 to 3 months. No impact seen currently, but dependent on FDA timing.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the large pharma wins, and can they be repeated? What is the API pricing environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Wins reflect long-standing customer relationships and pipeline work; capacity added about two years ago covers the business. Generic API pricing is stable, with differentiation via moving beyond generic API.

qa_highlights.question: Will sales and margins improve in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects H2 to improve HoH and gave no numerical guidance; cited Q2's approximately 9% sequential improvement as indication.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue from Surya Pette in FY26 and expected reopening timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Not disclosed. Management said the facility is smaller, non-GMP, and not a regular GMP plant; closure is early-stage and assessment is ongoing.

risks_watch: Surya Pette closure order: revenue at risk and reopening timeline not yet quantified; H2 YoY growth guidance could be affected if closure extends through Q3.
US FDA classification of recently inspected API and formulation facilities expected in 1 to 3 months; outcome drives H2 risk.
ADC customer destocking and NJ Bio utilisation; breakeven target depends on order recovery.
Inventory rose to Rs 7.3 bn from Rs 5.6 bn; cash conversion cycle needs to improve.
Specialty Chemicals decline in FY27 and generic pressure on legacy agrochemical products.
Raw material price increases affecting select API margins.
summary.management_tone: Confident on sequential recovery and H2 YoY growth, but guarded on Surya Pette, FDA outcomes and quantified guidance, repeatedly declining to give numbers. Specialty Chemicals outlook was cut explicitly.
key_quotes: Based on the visibility we have today, we continue to expect half-2 of FY 27 to deliver year-on-year growth on both revenue and EBITDA.
We are seeing a broader range of RFQs across payload and linkers, including opportunities that can potentially be developed and manufactured from India.

Q2 growth was achieved without contribution from early phase 3 supplies, supported by healthy demand for specialized nucleosides, amnesties and other building blocks for newer nucleic acid technologies.
